chapter: Harlem scene and race in music
title: His mother's disapproval of jazz and cabarets
summary: His mother was distressed by a cabaret with chorus girls, reflecting black community feelings about dignity.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I can't ... I can't say particularly. I do know -- and just speaking of jazz, I know that my mother -- or my father, well, he didn't care too much -- but my mother wasn't interested in my becoming a jazz musician. I think it was a little bit appalling to her that that I was making a living like this.

I remember on one occasion when she came to a club where I was playing with the Broadway Syncopators, incidentally, at this Capitol Cabaret that I spoke of, there was a chorus girl -- a line of chorus girls -- I don't think that before that particular time that my mother had ever been in a night-club or a cabaret, but she came because her son was playing in the band there. And she was very distressed that I was playing in a place with -- where girls were so scantily clad, you know?
And you know, jazz she was -- of course, this probably doesn't have a great deal to do with the Renaissance, but I think it might reflect the feeling of a lot of the black populace.

Yeah. The so-called guardians of taste, the leaders of the community -- looked upon jazz, no matter what they thought of it personally, and even if they may have liked it personally, they didn't think it was the kind of thing that was good for the black community to be known by?
I think they felt that it lacked ..

And as such, then, it would not be the kind of thing which Renaissance figures would take up, and of course, that's-- black historians who write about the Renaissance now say that the Renaissance was too attuned at that time to white views of black culture, even though black culture flourished a great deal.

And there was some wonderful things that were done. There was this aspect, which some historians point to now which would put these Renaissance figures in the same bracket as the general community or the guardians of taste, presumably, and regarding jazz as a
little bit below the standard that a rising community which wanted to improve itself should be associated with.
So there was a great deal of that at the time reflected in your mother's attitude.
Yeah. And of course you were pretty young then, and that must have bothered her.
That played a great part in it, you know, in her feelings about it, certainly.
